properties.areaDesc: City and Borough of Juneau
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 7:56AM AKDT until October 3 at 7:45AM AKDT by NWS Juneau AK
properties.description:
A second release from Suicide Basin has started and levels continue
to drop this afternoon. Levels on the Mendenhall have started to rise
but will continue to rise as the release continues.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by a glacier-dammed lake outburst is
expected.

* WHERE...The Mendenhall Lake And River near the Mendenhall Glacier
Recreation area, View Drive and below Back Loop bridge.

* WHEN...Until 745 AM AKDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of the area around Mendenhall Lake and along the
Mendenhall River is imminent. Water levels will continue to rise
and water temperatures will fall within the lake and river.

Impacts:
At 6.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the "causeway"
at the end of the trail.
At 7.7 feet: Nugget Falls trail begins to flood near the beginning of
the trail. Along the Mendenhall River some sections will experience
bank erosion resulting in dangerous tree fall. These conditions could
make floating the river more hazardous with the higher water levels.
At 9.0 feet: Water starts to cover Skaters Cabin Road between Skaters
Cabin and West Glacier Trailhead, also water will flow into the
Mendenhall Lake Campground.
At 10.0 feet: Water levels will inundate Mendenhall Campground with
up to 3 feet of water covering low areas as well as up to 1.5 feet of
water covering Skaters Cabin Road. Portions of West Glacier Trail
will be impassable. Areas along View Dr will start to flood and cause
minor flooding of yards. Closure of pedestrian pathways beneath
Brotherhood Bridge and the trail system on the west side of
Mendenhall River during outburst events.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 741 AM AKDT, gauge data reported a glacier-dammed lake
outburst. Flooding is expected to begin shortly, especially near
The Mendenhall Lake And River.
- The outburst flood forecast is based on an estimated volume of
water in the glacier dammed lake and an estimated release rate
based on previous events. The extent of water drainage within the
basin (partial or full) can vary widely between outburst flood
events and is a major source of uncertainty in the forecast,
particularly with regard to the peak flood stage.
- For Mendenhall Lake :
At 7:15am the stage was 5.0 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.
Forecast: A crest between 9.8 to 10.3 feet is expected around
2:00pm to 6:00pm Friday. Water levels will go above minor flood
stage around 10:00am Friday. Water levels will reach moderate
flood stage around 2:00pm to 6:00pm Friday.
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

The cold water temperatures can increase the threat of hypothermia
and lower the time required to cause hypothermia.

properties.areaDesc: Nuckolls, NE; Thayer, NE
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 10:53AM CDT until October 2 at 7:30PM CDT by NWS Hastings NE
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by earlier excessive rainfall is ongoing.

* WHERE...East Central Nuckolls County in south central Nebraska...
Northern Thayer County in south central Nebraska...

* WHEN...Until 730 PM CDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1034 AM CDT, various rainfall observations, automated river
gauges, and ground-truth reports from emergency management
personnel indicated that at least 3-5 inches of rain had fallen
within the Warning area over the last 48 hours, resulting in
continued flooding along area creeks and rivers. A river gauge
along the Little Blue River at Hebron reported a stage of 14.9
feet at 1015 AM CDT, which was 1.4 feet above minor flood stage
of 13.5 feet. As a result, minor flooding is ongoing both
upstream and downstream of Hebron along the Little Blue. Also, a
gauge along the Big Sandy Creek near Alexandria reported a stage
of 15.0 feet at 945 AM CDT, which was 0.5 feet above moderate
flood stage of 14.5 feet, and is actually the highest water level
there since 2015. This flooding has resulted in the closure of
state Highway 53 just south of Alexandria. Going forward, it is
likely that water levels will start to crest and eventually
slowly fall along the Little Blue River and Big Sandy Creek
sometime on Friday, but exact timing is still a bit uncertain as
upstream water continues to work into the area from the west.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Dry Creek, South Fork Big Sandy Creek, Little Blue River, Little
Sandy Creek, Oak Creek, Walnut Creek, Elk Creek, Turtle Creek,
Spring Creek, Balls Branch Rose Creek, Dry Sandy Creek and Big
Sandy Creek.
- Some locations that could experience flooding include...
Hebron, Davenport, Bruning, Alexandria, Carleton, Oak and
Belvidere.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

properties.description:

possible.

* WHERE...Much of central Iowa.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

heavy rain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Flooding is currently occurring in a few areas. Though rain has
mostly come to an end, rivers may continue to rise throughout the
day. Poor drainage and low lying areas may experience ponding.

streams, which may exceed flood stage. Of most concern include
but are not limited to portions of the following river basins...
South Skunk from Ames downstream, Des Moines from Des Moines
downstream, Raccoon downstream of U.S. Hwy 30, as well as the
Middle, South and Grand.

to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
The latest camera imagery from inside the basin showed a drop in
water level with a corresponding rise in water levels on Mendenhall
Lake overnight. This could be an
indication that a basin release has started. NWS hydrologists and
meteorologists along with their partners are
assessing and analyzing the information.

Water levels in the basin are around 200 ft below where it was
before the release in August so if it is a release, the crest should
be much lower.

Now is the time to start preparing for potential flooding impacts
along the Mendenhall Lake and River.
This statement will be updated within the next 24 hours so check
back on this possible evolving situation.

At 3:45am the stage was 4.5 feet.
Flood Stage is 9.0 feet.

properties.areaDesc: Tinian; Saipan
properties.headline: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 1 at 9:22PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
...TROPICAL STORM CHOI-WAN MOVING WEST INTO THE NORTHERN
MARIANAS, SOUTHEAST OF ALAMAGAN...

.NEW INFORMATION...
None.

.AREAS AFFECTED...
This local statement provides information and recommended actions
for people on Saipan, Tinian, Agrihan, Pagan and Alamagan in the
Commonwealth of the Northern Marianas.

.Watches/Warnings...
A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Tinian, Saipan, and
adjacent coastal waters.

A Tropical Storm Warning remains in effect for Alamagan, Pagan,
and Agrihan in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch remains in effect for Alamagan, Pagan, and Agrihan
in the CNMI.

A Typhoon Watch means that typhoon conditions, including winds of 74
mph or more, are possible within 48 hours.
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected within 24 hours.

A Flood Watch remains in effect for Tinian and Saipan. Please listen
closely for any Flash Flood Warnings that might be in effect for
your area.

Please check the latest public and marine forecasts for detailed
information about additional hazards.

.STORM INFORMATION...
At 7 PM ChST, the center of Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W) was
located near latitude 17.0N, longitude 146.4E. This was about 55
miles southeast of Alamagan, 90 miles south-southeast of Pagan,
and 260 miles north-northeast of Guam. Storm motion was west, 280
degrees, at 13 mph. Storm intensity was 45 mph.

.SITUATION OVERVIEW...
Tropical Storm Choi-Wan is expected to slow slightly as it
continues westward overnight, with the center passing to the south
of Alamagan early Friday morning. It is then expected to make a
turn toward the northwest, then north with a decrease in forward
speed through Friday. Then, Choi-wan looks to gradually turn to
the north-northeast on Saturday after it emerges west of the
northern islands. Choi-wan is forecast to intensify through
Friday, potentially becoming a typhoon late Friday night or early
Saturday morning.

This forecasted passage moving along the axis of the far northern
Marianas is still expected to prolong the duration of damaging
winds across the northern islands, likely leading to a lengthy
period of time of damaging to destructive tropical storm
conditions continuing into Sunday afternoon. As Choi-wan is
forecast to strengthen to a typhoon, there is a possibility for
typhoon-force conditions to develop somewhere along the far
northern Marianas. As such, a Typhoon Watch and Tropical Storm
Warning remain in effect for Alamagan, Pagan, and Agrihan. The
latest forecast track has shifted Choi-Wan farther west of the
islands, slightly decreasing this possibility.
properties.instruction:
Stay indoors during heavy rain and tropical storm-force wind
conditions associated with Tropical Storm Choi-wan (26W). Heed the
advice of your local emergency managers and officials, and
continue to monitor forecasts by the National Weather Service
office in Tiyan, Guam. Remain in sturdy shelter until the all-
clear is given.

Preparations for Tropical Storm Choi-wan should be complete, or
rapidly rushed to completion. Take small loose object indoors.
Remain in suitable shelter. If no concrete shelter is available,
look for a cave or something similar. Shelter in place until the
all-clear is given.

.WIND INFORMATION...
North to northeast winds of 15 to 25 mph will turn toward the
southeast and increase through Friday as Choi-wan moves west
across the northern CNMI and strengthens, potentially becoming a
typhoon Friday night to the west of Alamagan and Pagan as it turns
to the north. Tropical storm force winds of 39 to 50 mph look to
continue through Sunday. Depending on the track and intensity,
winds may increase to strong tropical storm-force of 58 to 65 mph
early Saturday morning. Typhoon force winds greater than 74 mph
look to remain possible during closest passage.

.COASTAL INUNDATION AND SURF INFORMATION...
Surf will initially build to 8 to 12 feet along east-facing reefs
through Friday morning, then spread along north and west-facing
reefs as the center moves north-northeast west of the northern
CNMI Friday night through Saturday night, increasing by several
feet during this time. As Choi-wan continues to strengthen, surf
will continue to increase, likely becoming dangerous by early next
week. Significant coastal erosion and some coastal inundation is
expected during Choi-wan's passage.

.OTHER STORM EFFECTS...
Periods of rain, widespread heavy showers and scattered thunderstorms
could produce rainfall totals of 10 to 16 inches by early Monday
morning, with up to 20 inches of rainfall possible near the center of
the system.

properties.areaDesc: Matagorda Islands; Brazoria Islands; Galveston Island; Bolivar Peninsula
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 1 at 5:45AM CDT until October 1 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Houston/Galveston TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Gulf-facing beaches, including the Matagorda
Peninsula, Brazoria County beaches, Galveston Island and the
Bolivar Peninsula.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard and away from rocks, jetties, and piers. If
caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against the
current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If
unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued October 1 at 8:43PM ChST until October 5 at 4:00AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 8 to
12 feet expected in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...North, west and south facing reefs of Guam and Rota.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, from 4 AM Friday to 4 AM
ChST Monday. For the High Rip Current Risk, from late tonight
through late Sunday night.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
Rip currents will be life threatening. Inexperienced swimmers
should remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions.
If caught in a rip current, relax and float. Don't swim against
the current. If able, swim in a direction following the shoreline.
If unable to escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 1 at 5:25AM CDT until October 2 at 9:12AM CDT by NWS Omaha/Valley NE
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in
Nebraska...

Platte River Near Louisville affecting Sarpy and Cass Counties.

Wahoo Creek At Ithaca affecting Saunders County.

Salt Creek Near Ashland affecting Saunders County.

...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Nebraska...

Salt Creek at Roca affecting Lancaster County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Salt Creek at Roca.

* WHEN...Until Friday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 19.5 feet, Roca road west of the gage site floods.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 4:40 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 1.8 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 19.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
this morning to a crest of 19.7 feet this afternoon. It will then
fall below flood stage late this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 19.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.7
feet on 07/04/1984.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at water.noaa.gov.

The next statement will be issued this afternoon at 530 PM CDT.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 1 at 12:29AM PDT until October 8 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS San Diego CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures in the
upper 90s to 106 expected. Nights will be very warm with low
temperatures mostly in the mid 60s to lower 70s.

* WHERE...San Bernardino and Riverside County Valleys-The Inland
Empire.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 8 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued September 30 at 7:58PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
With widespread colder weather across the Interior, another front
will bring light snow to portions of the area Wednesday night
through Thursday. Generally, around 1 to 3 inches are expected
around the Central & eastern Interior, generally from around the
Fairbanks Metro Area & eastward, although some isolated locations
could receive some locally marginally higher amounts, like toward
the Chena Recreational Area, Chena Hot Springs, the White
Mountains, & Fortymile Country. Take extra precautions when
driving around the Fairbanks area during the Thursday morning
commute as roads may be snow-covered & slippery. Drier weather
returns to the region by Friday.

NWSheadline: Light Accumulating Snow Wednesday Night & Thursday

properties.areaDesc: Potter, TX
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued September 30 at 10:34PM CDT until October 3 at 4:00AM CDT by NWS Amarillo TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Canadian River at Amarillo 19N affecting Potter County.

For the Canadian River...Amarillo 19N...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Canadian River at Amarillo 19N.

* WHEN...Until late Friday night.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Portions of Rosita Creek Flats Recreational
Area floods. Primitive campers and recreational vehicles are in
imminent danger. Dirt roads that lead to highway 287 from Rosita
Creek Flats are impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:00 PM CDT Wednesday the stage was 8.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 7.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 10:00 PM CDT Wednesday was 10.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 8.9 feet
tomorrow evening. It will then fall below flood stage Friday
afternoon.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 9.5
feet on 06/24/1996.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued Thursday afternoon at 400 PM CDT.

properties.areaDesc: Koror Palau Coastal Waters; Yap Coastal Waters; Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 1 at 12:15PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The latest forecasts from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center (JTWC) and
numerical guidance continues to strengthen Tropical Storm Choi-Wan
(26W) as it crosses the Marianas sometime this weekend, possibly
stalling or slowing to a crawl as it does so, becoming a typhoon by
the end of the weekend. Choi-Wan is then forecast to turn north and
accelerate somewhat during the early to middle portion of next week
while it continues strengthening, possibly into a major typhoon.

As all of this occurs, the west to southwest monsoon flow already
encompassing northern Palau (mainly near Koror) and western Yap State
will continue strengthening, with sustained winds of 15 to 20 knots
possible. Strong moisture pooling near the trough axis combined with
at least decent surface convergence should foster increasing shower
and thunderstorm coverage and intensity as we head into the weekend
and early next week. Current indications are for 3 to 6 inches of
rainfall, locally in excess of 8 inches being probable for northern
Palau and western Yap State. This could lead to some minor flooding
concerns and landslide potential, especially near Koror where the
steeper terrain is juxtaposed with the strong moisture pooling and
surface convergence.

As the winds increase, and Choi-Wan strengthens, seas and surf will
also increase. This could lead to hazardous conditions for the
northern reefs and potentially for small craft traversing the waters.

Residents across northern Palau and western Yap States are encouraged
to continue to follow forecast trends at www.weather.gov/gum and on
social media.

NWSheadline: INCREASING WINDS, SEAS, SURF, AND HEAVY RAINFALL THROUGH EARLY NEXT WEEK AS CHOI-WAN STRENGTHENS NEAR THE MARIANAS

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued September 30 at 3:46PM PDT until October 1 at 5:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Up to 1.1 ft of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Bayshore locations along the San Francisco Bay, San
Pablo Bay, and Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Now through 5 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. High tides will result in
flooding along coastal trails, cut off access to some low-
lying beaches and coastal areas, and bring water and waves
farther up the beach than typical.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tidal gauge, high tide
is expected to be 1.1 ft above normal (6.92 ft MLLW) at 2:58 PM
Thursday 10/01. These predictions include up to 0.7 ft of surge
that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat.
High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the
Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

properties.description:

drying on Saturday. Between Wednesday and Friday, snowfall totals
will range from 2 to 4 inches. Isolated locations under any
persistent heavier snow may see up to 6 inches.

tomorrow, but strongest Thursday night into Friday from Nuiqsut
to Kaktovik. Wind gusts will be up to 30 mph which may result in
areas of blowing/drifting snow, lowering visibility at times.
